full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadoth Hossain, J: This first appeal is directed against judgment and decree dated 31-7-1991 passed by the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) First Commercial Court, Chittagong in Money Suit No. 185 of 1987 dismissing the suit. 

 21. On conclusion of the hearing, learned judge of the trial court dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 31-7-1991. Being aggrieved thereby, the plaintiff-bank preferred this first appeal. 

 22. Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant submits that it has been clearly proved by evidence that defendant No.1 had opened LC through the plaintiff-bank, imported powder milk and released the same on an indemnity bond in collusion with defendant No. 2, but did not repay the outstanding loan. The trial court without proper assessment of evidence dismissed the suit by the impugned judgment and decree, which is liable to be set-aside. 

 24. Mr. Bhuiyan then submits that defendant No. 1 in his deposition stated that he did not open the LC and deposit money in the account and simply signed the papers according to the desire of defendant No. 2, which is unbelievable, contradictory and inconsistent. In cross-examination he (defendant No.1) stated that he had an account with Janata Bank, Chowdhury Hat Branch and defendant No. 2 was the Manager of the said branch and defendant No. 1 was engaged in export/import business through that branch and he established a good relation with defendant No. 2. Under the circumstances, a collusive transection between the defendants could easily be inferred. Over and above, defendant No. 1 failed to show repayment of the loan and, as such, it was incumbent upon the trial court to pass a decree for realization of the loan as claimed by the plaintiff-bank.
